newsitem.title: USA: U.S. aluminum premiums shoot up for spot loads.
newsitem.headline: U.S. aluminum premiums shoot up for spot loads.

text.p: Lengthening delivery times at domestic aluminum mills spurred spot premiums to 6.00 cents a lb and higher over LME cash, but the rising influx of Russian metal should deter any prolonged spike, traders said.
A merchant said lead times at North American mills for their Western grade P1020 metal has risen to 10 to 12 weeks, up from six to eight weeks a month ago.
Part of the problem was that metal was held up on railcars trapped in bad weather that hit the Pacific Northwest, earlier in the year, traders said.
Some 40 percent of U.S. aluminum production is located in the region.
Compounding the tightness is that U.S. aluminum producers themselves have become strong buyers of metal to top up their internal deliveries to integrated fabricating plants, traders added.
"They are clearly expecting more than a typically strong cyclical first quarter," one merchant noted.
Some consumers have been willing to pay premiums of 6.00 cents a lb and higher for prompt delivery within two weeks on small quantities of one, two or three truckloads.

"We have bought over and sold over six cents," one dealer said. "It's a window and the only thing that negates a quick fall off is the producers as such strong buyers and look to be net short for a while."
Traders said premiums on good-sized P1020 grade volume deals were still in the range of 5.25 to 5.75 cents a lb for March.

But more Russian metal was already entering the country, with some dealers able to entice consumers to take Russian A6 grade metal at about half a cent discount to the P1020 premiums in the U.S. Midwest.
And few boatloads of Russian A7E LME deliverable metal was also coming into the U.S. to fetch the same premiums at P1020 grade metal, traders said.
An LME broker said the 6.00 cents a lb premium deals were "one-off," but should attract a draw of A7E metal from LME warehouses.
"I expect to see a substantial drawdown of aluminum from LME warehouses in coming weeks," the broker added.
